title: Stand each girder's stop-end in the middle third of its span, clear of the beam
instruction: Today's pour stops in this bay. Stand one yellow stop-end upright across each of the two girder forms, square to it and on its floor, with all of it inside the middle third of the girder's span (between the column centres) and at least twice the cross beam's width (40 mm) clear of the cross beam's side. Then let go of both.
context: Formwork carpenters (O*NET 47-2031) and concrete finishers (47-2051): when a floor is poured in more than one go, carpenters fix a stop-end (bulkhead) across the beam forms where the day's pour will stop, and the finishers pour up to it, leaving a construction joint. The ACI 318 building code (26.5.6.2) places construction joints in floors within the middle third of the spans of slabs, beams and girders, where shear is lowest, and offsets a joint in a girder at least two times the width of any intersecting beam, measured from that beam's face: beside a beam that frames in, the girder carries that beam's load. Together the two rules leave one band on one side of the cross beam; the obvious mid-span spot is inside the middle third but too near the beam. The model is at 1:15: a 4.5 m span, 0.75 m wide girders and a 0.30 m wide cross beam.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. On the table is a 1:15 model of the beam formwork for one bay of a floor; the table is the forms' floor. Four kinds of thing are on it. (1) Columns: four grey concrete blocks, 40 x 40 x 40 mm, fixed, centred at x 14.0 and 44.0 cm, y +20.0 and -20.0 cm: the two girders' supports, 300 mm apart centre to centre. (2) Girder forms: two open troughs along x between the columns (x 16.0 to 42.0 cm), one each side of the midline, centred on y +20.0 and -20.0 cm, 50 mm wide inside. Each has two side forms of dark red-brown film-faced plywood, 10 mm thick and 25 mm tall, fixed: for the left girder the outer form spans y +22.5 to +23.5 cm and x 16.0 to 42.0 cm, and the inner form spans y +16.5 to +17.5 cm in two pieces, x 16.0 to 23.5 cm and x 25.5 to 42.0 cm, leaving the cross beam's mouth; the right girder is its mirror image. The columns stand in the troughs' ends. (3) Cross beam form: two side forms of the same plywood, 10 mm thick, 25 mm tall and 330 mm long along y (y -16.5 to +16.5 cm), fixed at x 22.5 to 23.5 cm and x 25.5 to 26.5 cm. Between them is the cross beam's trough, 20 mm wide, which opens into both girders; its side faces, at x 23.5 and 25.5 cm, are the faces the 40 mm offset is measured from. (4) Stop-ends: two loose, identical plywood boards with their faces painted yellow, each 40 mm long, 25 mm thick and 60 mm tall, 0.03 kg, plain rectangular blocks (either end may be down). Each stands upright on a 40 x 25 mm end on the table beside a girder: the left one centred at x 20.0 cm, y +32.0 cm with its 40 mm length turned 30 degrees anticlockwise from y (seen from above), the right one at x 20.0 cm, y -32.0 cm turned 30 degrees clockwise. A stop-end is 10 mm shorter than a trough is wide and stands 35 mm above the side forms. Derived, not marked on the table: the middle third of each girder's span is x 24.0 to 34.0 cm; 40 mm clear of the cross beam is x 29.5 cm or more on its far side and x 19.5 cm or less on its near side (outside the middle third). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged on the end state from the stop-ends' poses and the grippers' points (in a real trial: a tape from the column centres and the cross beam's faces, and a top photo). A stop-end's 'outline' is its shadow seen from above. It is 'over' a girder when its centre, seen from above, lies between that girder's column faces (x 16.0 to 42.0 cm) and its side forms' inside faces (y +17.5 to +22.5 cm, or -17.5 to -22.5 cm), at any height. It 'stands across' that girder when all of these hold: upright (its 60 mm side within 10 degrees of vertical); on the floor (its lowest point at most 5 mm above the table); square (its 40 mm length, seen from above, within 10 degrees of y, across the trough); inside the trough (its outline between the column faces and the side forms' inside faces, within 2 mm); and let go (both grippers' finger zones at least 20 mm from it). A gripper's 'finger zone' is every point within a radius of the line from the point between its finger tips to 38 mm back up the gripper; the radius reaches a finger's outer corner whichever way the gripper is turned: the square root of (half the finger gap + 10 mm)^2 + (20 mm)^2, so 60 mm fully open and 22 mm closed. A stop-end's place is its whole outline, not its centre: 'in the middle third' means its outline lies within x 24.0 to 34.0 cm; 'clear of the cross beam' means its outline is at least 40 mm (twice the cross beam's 20 mm width) from the cross beam's nearer side face, which inside the middle third means its outline starts at x 29.5 cm or further. Each stop-end over a girder scores 0.5 if it stands across it, in the middle third and clear of the cross beam (its outline within x 29.5 to 34.0 cm); 0.25 if it stands across it in the middle third but less than 40 mm from the cross beam (this includes one standing partly in front of the cross beam's mouth, its outline starting at x 24.0 to 25.5 cm); 0 otherwise (lying or leaning, lifted, turned more than 10 degrees, astride a form, still held, partly outside the middle third, near a column, across the whole of the cross beam's mouth). Each girder scores the worst of the stop-ends over it, and 0 if none is over it (one left on the table, in the cross beam's trough or on a column). Score = left girder + right girder. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 (for example both stop-ends centred at mid-span, x 29.0 cm, give 0.25 + 0.25 = 0.5; one in the band and one at mid-span 0.75). Limits are inclusive. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s with neither end of either stop-end moving more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, let go is taken as met.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with the simulator's default friction; the columns and forms are fixed and the table is the forms' floor (no deck, bars or concrete). A real stop-end is cut to the form's width and depth, nailed and sealed to it and slotted for the bars; here it is a free-standing block 10 mm shorter than the trough is wide, taller than the forms (60 vs 25 mm) and thicker (25 mm) so a gripper can hold it above them.
reset_notes: Stand the two stop-ends back upright on the table: the left one centred at x 20.0 cm, y +32.0 cm with its 40 mm length turned 30 degrees anticlockwise from y, the right one at x 20.0 cm, y -32.0 cm turned 30 degrees clockwise. The columns and forms are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
